abstract: |
  This report builds a global balanced index fund for a local investor under a strict mandate: long-only, quarterly rebalancing, at most 25% in bonds, 75% in equities, 15% in commodities, 60% offshore and 35% in any single asset, using only assets with at least five years of data. Using monthly returns since 2010 on global and local equities, bonds and commodities, we compare a minimum-volatility portfolio, a mean-variance portfolio and a static balanced mix from 2020 to 2026. All three meet the mandate at every rebalance. The optimised portfolios did not beat the simple static mix: it had the highest Sharpe ratio, while the mean-variance portfolio, concentrated in a few past winners, suffered the deepest drawdown. Whatever the method, equities drive more than 80% of portfolio risk.
---

```{r functions, include=FALSE}
# All functions used in this report (the same functions as in the code/ folder),
# defined here so the document knits on its own.

# Month-end returns from a daily total return index (TRI levels)
Monthly_From_TRI <- function(df) {

  df %>%
    mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%m")) %>%
    group_by(Name, YM) %>% filter(date == max(date)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    group_by(Name) %>% arrange(date) %>%
    mutate(Return = TRI / lag(TRI) - 1) %>% ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(Return)) %>%
    select(date, Name, Return)

}

# Monthly 10-year bond returns from yields: carry minus duration x yield change
Bond_TRI <- function(Yields) {

  Yields %>%
    mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%m")) %>%
    group_by(Name, YM) %>% filter(date == max(date)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    group_by(Name) %>% arrange(date) %>%
    mutate(y = TRI / 100,
           D = ifelse(abs(y) < 1e-4, 10, (1 - (1 + y)^-10) / y),
           Return = lag(y) / 12 - lag(D) * (y - lag(y))) %>%
    ungroup() %>% filter(!is.na(Return)) %>%
    select(date, Name, Return)

}

# Constrained optimal weights at one rebalance date (quadprog)
Optim_Weights <- function(RebDate, Rets_M, Info, Type = "MinVol", WindowStart = ymd(20100101),
                          MinObs = 60, Lambda = 4, Max_Single = 0.35,
                          Max_Bonds = 0.25, Max_Equity = 0.75, Max_Commod = 0.15, Max_Global = 0.60) {

  # Expanding window from 2010; only assets with at least 5 years (60 months) of data
  Window <- Rets_M %>% filter(date >= WindowStart, date <= RebDate)
  Eligible <- Window %>% group_by(Name) %>%
    summarise(N = sum(!is.na(Return)), .groups = "drop") %>% filter(N >= MinObs) %>% pull(Name)

  R <- Window %>% filter(Name %in% Eligible) %>% spread(Name, Return) %>% select(-date)
  A <- Info %>% filter(Name %in% colnames(R)) %>% arrange(match(Name, colnames(R)))

  Mu <- sapply(R, function(x) exp(mean(log(1 + x), na.rm = TRUE)) - 1)          # geometric mean
  Sigma <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(cov(R, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))$mat)  # positive definite
  N <- ncol(R)

  # Constraints: sum = 1 | w >= 0 | w <= max | class and region caps
  Amat <- cbind(1, diag(N), -diag(N),
                -as.numeric(A$Class == "Bonds"), -as.numeric(A$Class == "Equity"),
                -as.numeric(A$Class == "Commodity"), -as.numeric(A$Region == "Global"))
  bvec <- c(1, rep(0, N), rep(-Max_Single, N), -Max_Bonds, -Max_Equity, -Max_Commod, -Max_Global)

  if (Type == "MinVol") { Dmat <- 2 * Sigma; dvec <- rep(0, N) } else { Dmat <- Lambda * Sigma; dvec <- Mu }

  w <- quadprog::solve.QP(Dmat, dvec, Amat, bvec, meq = 1)$solution
  w[abs(w) < 1e-6] <- 0

  tibble(date = RebDate, Name = colnames(R), Weight = w / sum(w))

}

# Backtest rebalance weights on monthly returns.
# lag_weights = FALSE: with monthly data, quarter-end weights apply from the next month's return.
Port_Return <- function(W, Rets_M, Label) {

  W_xts <- W %>% tbl_xts(cols_to_xts = Weight, spread_by = Name)
  W_xts[is.na(W_xts)] <- 0

  R_xts <- Rets_M %>% filter(Name %in% colnames(W_xts), date > min(W$date)) %>%
    tbl_xts(cols_to_xts = Return, spread_by = Name)
  R_xts[is.na(R_xts)] <- 0
  W_xts <- W_xts[, colnames(R_xts)]

  P <- rmsfuns::Safe_Return.portfolio(R = R_xts, weights = W_xts, lag_weights = FALSE,
                                      verbose = TRUE, geometric = TRUE)

  list(Ret = P$returns %>% xts_tbl() %>% setNames(c("date", "Return")) %>%
         mutate(date = as.Date(date), Name = Label),
       BOP = P$BOP.Weight)

}

# Check the mandate limits for a set of weights at each date
Check_Limits <- function(W, Info) {

  W %>% left_join(Info, by = "Name") %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(Sum = sum(Weight), Max_Single = max(Weight),
              Bonds = sum(Weight[Class == "Bonds"]), Equity = sum(Weight[Class == "Equity"]),
              Commodity = sum(Weight[Class == "Commodity"]), Global = sum(Weight[Region == "Global"]),
              N_Assets = sum(Weight > 0), .groups = "drop")

}

# Share of portfolio variance from each asset at one rebalance date: RC_i = w_i (Sigma w)_i / (w' Sigma w)
Risk_Contrib <- function(W, Rets_M, Info, RebDate, Label, WindowStart = ymd(20100101)) {

  w <- W %>% filter(date == RebDate, Weight > 0)
  R <- Rets_M %>% filter(Name %in% w$Name, date >= WindowStart, date <= RebDate) %>%
    spread(Name, Return) %>% select(all_of(w$Name))
  Sigma <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(cov(R, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"))$mat)
  MRC <- as.numeric(Sigma %*% w$Weight)

  tibble(Port = Label, Name = w$Name, Weight = w$Weight,
         Risk_Share = w$Weight * MRC / sum(w$Weight * MRC)) %>%
    left_join(Info, by = "Name")

}

# Average one-way turnover per rebalance
Turnover <- function(W) {

  W %>% complete(date, Name, fill = list(Weight = 0)) %>%
    group_by(Name) %>% arrange(date) %>% mutate(d = abs(Weight - lag(Weight))) %>%
    group_by(date) %>% summarise(T = sum(d, na.rm = TRUE) / 2, .groups = "drop") %>%
    summarise(Turnover = mean(T[-1])) %>% pull()

}
```

```{r data_prep, include=FALSE}
# Data (this question folder holds its own copy in data/)
MSCI <- read_rds("data/MSCI_Indexes.rds")
Bond_Yields <- read_rds("data/Global_Bond_Yields.rds")
Commods <- read_rds("data/Commodities.rds")
LCL_Yield_Proxies <- read_rds("data/Monthly_LCL_Yield_Indexes.rds")
Idx_Daily <- read_rds("data/Index_Returns_Daily.rds")

Global_Eq <- Monthly_From_TRI(MSCI %>% filter(Name %in% c("MSCI_USA", "MSCI_EU", "MSCI_Jap", "MSCI_EM")))
Global_Bonds <- Bond_TRI(Bond_Yields %>% filter(Name %in% c("US_10Yr", "Germany_10Yr", "UK_10Yr")))
Commod_M <- Monthly_From_TRI(Commods %>% filter(Name %in% c("Bcom_Index", "Gold")))

Local_Eq <- Idx_Daily %>%
  filter(Tickers %in% c("J200", "J201", "STXMOMJ433", "STXVALJ433", "STXLVLJ433")) %>%
  mutate(Name = recode(Tickers, J200 = "SA_Large", J201 = "SA_Mid", STXMOMJ433 = "SA_Momentum",
                       STXVALJ433 = "SA_Value", STXLVLJ433 = "SA_LowVol")) %>%
  mutate(YM = format(date, "%Y%m")) %>% group_by(Name, YM) %>%
  summarise(date = max(date), Return = prod(1 + Returns) - 1, n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(Name) %>% filter(!(row_number() == 1 & n < 15)) %>% ungroup() %>%   # drop partial first month
  select(date, Name, Return)

Local_Yield <- LCL_Yield_Proxies %>%
  mutate(Name = recode(Tickers, ALBITR = "SA_Bonds", CILITR = "SA_ILB", J253 = "SA_Property")) %>%
  select(date, Name, Return = Returns)

Rets_M <- bind_rows(Global_Eq, Global_Bonds, Commod_M, Local_Eq, Local_Yield) %>%
  mutate(date = ceiling_date(date, "month") - days(1)) %>%
  filter(date >= ymd(20100131), date <= ymd(20260930))

Info <- tribble(
  ~Name,          ~Class,      ~Region,
  "MSCI_USA",     "Equity",    "Global",
  "MSCI_EU",      "Equity",    "Global",
  "MSCI_Jap",     "Equity",    "Global",
  "MSCI_EM",      "Equity",    "Global",
  "US_10Yr",      "Bonds",     "Global",
  "Germany_10Yr", "Bonds",     "Global",
  "UK_10Yr",      "Bonds",     "Global",
  "Bcom_Index",   "Commodity", "Global",
  "Gold",         "Commodity", "Global",
  "SA_Large",     "Equity",    "Local",
  "SA_Mid",       "Equity",    "Local",
  "SA_Momentum",  "Equity",    "Local",
  "SA_Value",     "Equity",    "Local",
  "SA_LowVol",    "Equity",    "Local",
  "SA_Property",  "Equity",    "Local",
  "SA_Bonds",     "Bonds",     "Local",
  "SA_ILB",       "Bonds",     "Local")

# Rebalancing and weights
Reb_Dates <- Rets_M %>% distinct(date) %>%
  filter(month(date) %in% c(3, 6, 9, 12), date >= ymd(20191231), date < max(date)) %>% pull(date)

W_MinVol  <- map_df(Reb_Dates, ~ Optim_Weights(.x, Rets_M, Info, Type = "MinVol"))
W_MeanVar <- map_df(Reb_Dates, ~ Optim_Weights(.x, Rets_M, Info, Type = "MeanVar"))

Static <- tribble(~Name, ~Weight,
  "SA_Large", 0.20, "SA_Mid", 0.10, "SA_Property", 0.05,
  "MSCI_USA", 0.13, "MSCI_EU", 0.06, "MSCI_Jap", 0.02, "MSCI_EM", 0.04,
  "SA_Bonds", 0.12, "SA_ILB", 0.03, "US_10Yr", 0.05, "Germany_10Yr", 0.03, "UK_10Yr", 0.02,
  "Gold", 0.08, "Bcom_Index", 0.07)
W_Static <- map_df(Reb_Dates, ~ Static %>% mutate(date = .x))

# Backtest
P1 <- Port_Return(W_MinVol, Rets_M, "Min Volatility")
P2 <- Port_Return(W_MeanVar, Rets_M, "Mean-Variance")
P3 <- Port_Return(W_Static, Rets_M, "Static Balanced")
Ports <- bind_rows(P1$Ret, P2$Ret, P3$Ret)
Ports_xts <- Ports %>% mutate(Name = gsub(" |-", "_", Name)) %>% tbl_xts(cols_to_xts = Return, spread_by = Name)
Ports_xts <- Ports_xts[, c("Min_Volatility", "Mean_Variance", "Static_Balanced")]

Perf <- rbind(table.AnnualizedReturns(Ports_xts, scale = 12),
              maxDrawdown(Ports_xts), ES(Ports_xts, p = .95, method = "modified"))
Last <- max(Reb_Dates)
Drift <- P1$BOP %>% xts_tbl() %>% gather(Name, W, -date) %>% left_join(Info, by = "Name") %>%
  group_by(date) %>% summarise(Global = sum(W[Region == "Global"]), Bonds = sum(W[Class == "Bonds"]), Max = max(W)) %>%
  summarise(across(-date, max))
RCs <- bind_rows(Risk_Contrib(W_MinVol, Rets_M, Info, Last, "Min Volatility"),
                 Risk_Contrib(W_MeanVar, Rets_M, Info, Last, "Mean-Variance"),
                 Risk_Contrib(W_Static, Rets_M, Info, Last, "Static Balanced"))
RC_Class <- RCs %>% group_by(Port, Class) %>% summarise(Weight = sum(Weight), Risk = sum(Risk_Share), .groups = "drop")

pc <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(format(round(100 * x, d), nsmall = d), "\\%")
```

# Introduction \label{Introduction}

A global balanced fund has to do two things at once: spread risk across regions and asset classes, and stay inside a mandate. This report builds such a fund for a local investor. The mandate is long-only, rebalanced quarterly, with at most 25% in bonds and credit, 75% in equities, 15% in commodities, 60% offshore and 35% in any single asset. Assets need at least five years of data, and the covariance matrix is estimated on monthly data from 2010.

We compare three ways of setting the weights: a minimum-volatility (MinVol) portfolio, a mean-variance (MeanVar) portfolio [@markowitz1952], and a static balanced mix that does not use the data at all. The short answer is that the optimisers did not beat the simple mix, and that, whatever the method, equities carry most of the risk.

# Data and Methodology \label{Data}

The universe has 17 assets (Table \ref{tab:assets}): four MSCI equity regions, three 10-year government bonds (US, Germany and UK), the Bloomberg Commodity index and gold offshore; and locally the Top 40 (Large Caps), Mid Caps, three factor indexes (Momentum, Value and Low Volatility), Listed Property, the ALBI and inflation-linked bonds. Listed Property is classed as equity. All returns are monthly, from January 2010 to September 2026.

The global bond files contain yields, not prices, so we build a total return index from them. Each month's return is the carry minus the price effect of the yield change:
$$
r_t \approx \frac{y_{t-1}}{12} - D_{t-1}\,\Delta y_t, \qquad D = \frac{1-(1+y)^{-10}}{y},
$$
where $D$ is the (modified) duration of a 10-year bond. This approximation captures the 2022 bond crash: the German, UK and US proxies lost about 23%, 21% and 17% that year.

```{r assets, results = "asis"}
Rets_M %>% left_join(Info, by = "Name") %>% group_by(Name, Class, Region) %>%
  summarise(Start = format(min(date), "%Y-%m"), Months = n(),
            `Return (\\%)` = 100 * (prod(1 + Return)^(12 / n()) - 1),
            `Vol (\\%)` = 100 * sd(Return) * sqrt(12), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Region, Class, Name) %>% mutate(Name = gsub("_", " ", Name)) %>%
  Print_Table(Caption = "Asset universe: annualised return and volatility over each asset's full sample \\label{tab:assets}", Digits = 1)
```

At each quarter-end from December 2019 we estimate the mean vector $\mu$ (geometric mean) and the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ on an expanding window from 2010, so the look-back is always at least ten years. Assets with fewer than 60 months of data are excluded; as a result Low Volatility never enters, Momentum enters in 2022 and Value in 2023. Because local data start later, $\Sigma$ is estimated on pairwise-complete data and adjusted to the nearest positive definite matrix. The two optimised portfolios solve

$$
\text{MinVol:}\; \min_w\, w'\Sigma w \qquad\qquad \text{MeanVar:}\; \max_w\, w'\mu - \frac{\lambda}{2}\, w'\Sigma w, \quad \lambda = 4,
$$
subject to $\sum_i w_i = 1$, $0 \le w_i \le 0.35$, and the class and regional caps above. The static mix holds 60% equity, 25% bonds and 15% commodities, with 50% offshore. Weights are applied from the month after each rebalance, and drift with returns in between.

# Results \label{Results}

## Meeting the mandate

Table \ref{tab:limits} shows the largest exposure each portfolio took at any rebalance date. All limits are met. The optimisers push straight to the binding constraints: MinVol fills the bond, commodity and offshore caps, because these assets lower volatility, while MeanVar fills the single-asset cap and holds only a handful of assets.

```{r limits, results = "asis"}
bind_rows(Check_Limits(W_MinVol, Info) %>% mutate(Portfolio = "Min Volatility"),
          Check_Limits(W_MeanVar, Info) %>% mutate(Portfolio = "Mean-Variance"),
          Check_Limits(W_Static, Info) %>% mutate(Portfolio = "Static Balanced")) %>%
  group_by(Portfolio) %>%
  summarise(`Max single` = max(Max_Single), Bonds = max(Bonds), Equity = max(Equity),
            Commodity = max(Commodity), Global = max(Global), `Max assets` = max(N_Assets)) %>%
  arrange(match(Portfolio, c("Min Volatility", "Mean-Variance", "Static Balanced"))) %>%
  Print_Table(Caption = "Largest exposure at any rebalance date (limits: 0.35, 0.25, 0.75, 0.15, 0.60) \\label{tab:limits}")
```

Figure \ref{fig:weights} shows how the weights moved. MinVol stays well spread, with a large offshore bond and commodity block. MeanVar is much more concentrated: at the latest rebalance it holds only `r sum(W_MeanVar$date == Last & W_MeanVar$Weight > 0)` assets, led by US equities at the 35% cap, local Large Caps and the ALBI.

```{r weights, fig.cap = "Portfolio weights by region and asset class at each rebalance \\label{fig:weights}", fig.height = 5.5}
g <- bind_rows(W_MinVol %>% mutate(Port = "Min Volatility"), W_MeanVar %>% mutate(Port = "Mean-Variance")) %>%
  left_join(Info, by = "Name") %>% mutate(Group = paste(Region, Class)) %>%
  group_by(Port, date, Group) %>% summarise(Weight = sum(Weight), .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot() + geom_area(aes(date, Weight, fill = Group)) +
  facet_wrap(~Port, ncol = 1) + fmxdat::theme_fmx(legend.size = ggpts(25)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) + labs(x = "", y = "", fill = "")
fmxdat::finplot(g, y.pct = TRUE)
```

## Performance

Table \ref{tab:perf} and Figure \ref{fig:cum} compare the three portfolios from January 2020. The static mix had the best return and the best Sharpe ratio, at almost the same volatility as MinVol. MeanVar was the worst on every risk measure: its drawdown of `r pc(Perf[4, 2])` was much deeper than the others, because it bet on the few assets with the best history. This is the well-known estimation-error problem: optimisers treat noisy historical means as if they were known, and simple mixes are hard to beat out of sample [@demiguel2009].

```{r perf, results = "asis"}
tibble(Measure = c("Annualised return", "Annualised volatility", "Sharpe ratio", "Maximum drawdown", "Modified ES (95%)"),
       `Min Volatility` = Perf[, 1], `Mean-Variance` = Perf[, 2], `Static Balanced` = Perf[, 3]) %>%
  mutate(across(-Measure, ~ ifelse(Measure == "Sharpe ratio", sprintf("%.2f", .), sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * .)))) %>%
  Print_Table(Caption = "Backtest performance, January 2020 to September 2026 (monthly returns) \\label{tab:perf}")
```

```{r cum, fig.cap = "Cumulative return of the three portfolios \\label{fig:cum}", fig.height = 4}
g <- Ports %>% group_by(Name) %>% arrange(date) %>% mutate(Cum = cumprod(1 + Return)) %>% ungroup() %>%
  ggplot() + geom_line(aes(date, Cum, color = Name), linewidth = 0.9) +
  fmxdat::theme_fmx(legend.size = ggpts(25)) + labs(x = "", y = "Growth of R1")
fmxdat::finplot(g)
```

## Where the risk comes from

Weights can be misleading. The share of portfolio variance from asset $i$ is
$$
RC_i = \frac{w_i\,(\Sigma w)_i}{w'\Sigma w}, \qquad \sum_i RC_i = 1 .
$$
Table \ref{tab:risk} shows that at the latest rebalance equities make up 60--65% of each portfolio but more than 80% of its risk, while bonds carry 25% of the weight but only 5--12% of the risk. A "balanced" fund is, in risk terms, still mainly an equity fund. An equal-risk-contribution portfolio would spread risk more evenly [@maillard2010].

```{r risk, results = "asis"}
RC_Class %>% mutate(Value = sprintf("%.0f%% / %.0f%%", 100 * Weight, 100 * Risk)) %>%
  select(Port, Class, Value) %>% spread(Class, Value) %>%
  arrange(match(Port, c("Min Volatility", "Mean-Variance", "Static Balanced"))) %>%
  rename(Portfolio = Port) %>%
  Print_Table(Caption = paste0("Weight / share of risk by asset class at the ", format(Last, "%B %Y"), " rebalance \\label{tab:risk}"))
```

## Practical points

Two practical issues matter for running the fund. First, the limits only hold at rebalance dates. Between rebalances, MinVol's offshore weight drifted up to `r pc(Drift$Global)` and its largest position to `r pc(Drift$Max)`, above the 60% and 35% caps. In practice the fund should target slightly below each cap, or rebalance early when a cap is breached. Second, costs are low: average one-way turnover is `r pc(Turnover(W_MinVol))` per quarter for MinVol and `r pc(Turnover(W_MeanVar))` for MeanVar, because the expanding window changes slowly.

# Conclusion \label{Conclusion}

All three portfolios meet the mandate, but the simplest one did best. The static 60/25/15 mix had the highest Sharpe ratio, the minimum-volatility portfolio matched its risk without beating its return, and the mean-variance portfolio was concentrated and fragile. We would therefore recommend a static or minimum-volatility core, with weights set slightly inside the limits to allow for drift. The results have limits: global assets are in US dollars and local assets in rand, with no currency conversion; the global bond returns are a duration approximation; and the local series are short, so the covariance matrix leans heavily on global data. Shrinking the covariance matrix, or targeting equal risk contributions, are natural next steps.
